Row.Text: Strategic Resources That Matter

Strategic resources matter again. A unit that needs Horses, Ivory, Iron, Niter, Hardwood, Oil, Coal or Rubber fights weaker and trains slower while its owner has none of that resource, and each one you do hold still adds the game's own bonus. Lose the last one and the penalty comes back a turn later. Past six, the count keeps adding strength. Game setup options set the penalty, up to locking a unit behind its resource, switch the late bonus and can give every Modern unit a second resource. Single-player. In multiplayer, losing a resource does not bring the penalty back until that player gains a resource.

Unsupplied Units

How much weaker and slower to train a unit is while its owner has none of the strategic resource it needs. The two locked values add a lock on top of the Harsh penalty: the unit can't be trained or bought at all without its resource. Units already in the field are never locked; independent powers and city-states are never affected.
Off
No penalty. Each resource you hold still adds the game's own bonus.
Light
-2 Combat Strength, and 20% less Production toward the unit.
Standard
-3 Combat Strength, and 33% less Production toward the unit (half as long again to train).
Harsh
-5 Combat Strength, and 50% less Production toward the unit (twice as long to train).
Locked: training
The Harsh penalty in the field, and a unit that needs a strategic resource can't be trained or bought while its owner has none of it. Upgrading into it stays free.
Locked: training and upgrade
The Harsh penalty in the field, and a unit that needs a strategic resource can't be trained, bought or upgraded into while its owner has none of it.
Strategic Resources Past Six
The game's +1 Combat Strength for each of a strategic resource you hold stops at six. With this on, units gain +1 more at 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 and 20.
Off
The bonus stops at six, as in the base game.
On
+1 Combat Strength at 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 and 20 of a resource.
Modern Supply Chains

In the Modern age, every unit that needs a strategic resource needs a second one as well: Coal for the steel in guns, armour and battleships, Niter for the guns of light warships, Oil for aircraft. Each missing resource costs the full penalty, and under the locked values the unit needs both to be trained. Off by default: it's a hard game.
Off
Each Modern unit needs one resource, as in the other ages.
On

Field artillery needs Niter and Coal; the heavier artillery, armour and battleships Oil and Coal; light warships Coal and Niter; aircraft Rubber and Oil. The Cuirassier needs Horses and Niter, the Ship of the Line Hardwood and Niter, the Submarine Oil and Rubber.
Strategic Resources

A military unit that needs {LOC_RESOURCE_HORSES_NAME}, {LOC_RESOURCE_IVORY_NAME}, {LOC_RESOURCE_IRON_NAME}, {LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME}, {LOC_RESOURCE_HARDWOOD_NAME}, {LOC_RESOURCE_OIL_NAME}, {LOC_RESOURCE_COAL_NAME} or {LOC_RESOURCE_RUBBER_NAME} fights weaker and trains slower while its owner has none of that resource. Nothing is forbidden unless {LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_NAME} is set to one of its locked values: see the last chapter.
Without the resource

A unit whose owner has none of its resource loses Combat Strength on each strength it has (melee, and ranged and bombard where it has them), and its city puts less Production toward training it. The {LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_NAME} option in game setup sets how much:

[B]{LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_LIGHT}:[/B] -2 Combat Strength, 20% less Production.[N][B]{LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_STANDARD}[/B] (the default): -3 Combat Strength, 33% less Production, so the unit takes half as long again to train.[N][B]{LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_HARSH}:[/B] -5 Combat Strength, 50% less Production, twice as long to train.[N][B]{LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_OFF}:[/B] no penalty.[N][B]{LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_LOCKED}[/B] and [B]{LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_LOCKED_UPGRADE}:[/B] the Harsh penalty, and the unit locked while you have none of its resource (see the last chapter).
The combat preview shows the penalty on a line of its own, such as "-3 Unsupplied: no {LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME}", and the unit panel says so under the unit's stats.
What counts as having a resource

You have a strategic resource when a tile of yours carries it with its improvement in place (the one your city builds when it grows onto the tile), or when a trade route brings it from another civilization's settlement, from the turn the route is made. Each such tile or route counts as one of that resource.
A resource granted off the map, with no tile behind it, does not count.
Losing a resource

Gaining a resource lifts the penalty the moment it arrives. Losing your last one, to pillage, to a tile changing hands or in any other way, brings the penalty back one turn later, for you and for the AI players alike.

A war with a trade partner ends the route: the resources it brought are gone at once, and so is their protection. As long as a player holds at least one of a resource, the units that need it fight and train as usual.
Past six

The game gives +1 Combat Strength for each of a strategic resource you hold, up to six. With the {LOC_SR_SETUP_LATE_CURVE_NAME} option on (the default), more keep adding: +1 Combat Strength at 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 and 20, on the units the game's own bonus covers. The combat preview shows it as one line beside the game's own, such as "+1 {LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME}: 8 or more". The Khmer's and Maurya's war elephants count Ivory the same way: +1 per Ivory up to six from the mod, and the steps past six with this option.
Which units need what
A civilization's unique unit needs what the unit it replaces needs.

[B]{LOC_AGE_EXPLORATION_NAME}[/B][N]{LOC_RESOURCE_HORSES_NAME}: cavalry (Courser, Knight, Lancer and their unique versions)[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_IRON_NAME}: infantry from the second tier (Man-At-Arms, Pikeman and their unique versions)[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME}: siege from the third tier (Bombard, Hwacha)[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_HARDWOOD_NAME} or {LOC_RESOURCE_PITCH_NAME}: heavy warships from the second tier (Carrack, Galleon and their unique versions)

[B]{LOC_AGE_MODERN_NAME}[/B][N]{LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME}: field artillery (Field Cannon, Field Gun)[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_OIL_NAME}: the heavier artillery (AT Gun, Mortar, Howitzer, Assault Gun), armour (Landship, Tank and their unique versions) and battleships (Dreadnought, Battleship and their unique versions)[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_COAL_NAME}: light warships (Ironclad, Cruiser, Destroyer, Barbary Corsair)[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_RUBBER_NAME}: aircraft[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_HORSES_NAME}: Cuirassier[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_HARDWOOD_NAME}: Ship of the Line[N]{LOC_RESOURCE_OIL_NAME}: Submarine

Free of any requirement: the Warrior line and the Scout, ranged infantry (Archer, Crossbowman, Arquebusier), the Catapult and the Trebuchet, the Cog and the Ship of the Line, the Cuirassier, the Submarine, and Modern infantry, so every player can always defend.
Modern supply chains

With {LOC_SR_SETUP_CHAINS_NAME} on (off by default), every Modern unit that needs a resource needs a second one too: field artillery {LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME} and {LOC_RESOURCE_COAL_NAME}, the heavier artillery {LOC_RESOURCE_OIL_NAME} and {LOC_RESOURCE_COAL_NAME}, armour and battleships {LOC_RESOURCE_OIL_NAME} and {LOC_RESOURCE_COAL_NAME}, light warships {LOC_RESOURCE_COAL_NAME} and {LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME}, Cuirassier {LOC_RESOURCE_HORSES_NAME} and {LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME}, Ship of the Line {LOC_RESOURCE_HARDWOOD_NAME} and {LOC_RESOURCE_NITER_NAME}, Submarine {LOC_RESOURCE_OIL_NAME} and {LOC_RESOURCE_RUBBER_NAME}, aircraft {LOC_RESOURCE_RUBBER_NAME} and {LOC_RESOURCE_OIL_NAME}. Each missing resource costs the full penalty, so a unit short of both fights at twice it, and under the locked values the unit can't be trained without both. Iron isn't found on Modern maps, so Coal stands for steel.

Locked Units
Free Tier-Up by Kills

The Sengoku's Samurai move up a tier by themselves after three kills. With this on, that happens whether or not you hold Iron. Turning it off only matters with Unsupplied Units on "Locked: training and upgrade": kills stop moving them up, and they upgrade like any other unit, which needs Iron. Off also overrides any other mod's change to those kill counts.
Off
With Unsupplied Units on "Locked: training and upgrade", kills don't move a Samurai up. It upgrades like any other unit, and only while you hold Iron.
On
A Samurai moves up after three kills at each tier, Iron or not, as in the base game.

Gated units

With {LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_NAME} on one of its locked values, a unit that needs a strategic resource cannot be trained or bought while you have none of it: it stays in the production list, greyed out, until you get some, and it is locked again the moment your last one goes. Under {LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_LOCKED_UPGRADE} no unit can be upgraded into it either, and a commander's Upgrade All leaves it as it is; under {LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_LOCKED} upgrades stay free.

Units already in the field are never locked: they keep fighting, at the {LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_HARSH} penalty, and they heal as usual. A civilization's unique unit is locked like the unit it replaces. The units free of any requirement stay free, so every player can always defend. Independent powers and city-states are never locked.

The Sengoku's Samurai move up to their second and third tier by themselves, after three kills at each tier. With {LOC_SR_SETUP_KILL_TIERS_NAME} on (the default), that step doesn't need {LOC_RESOURCE_IRON_NAME}, even under {LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_LOCKED_UPGRADE}. With it off and {LOC_SR_SETUP_UNSUPPLIED_LOCKED_UPGRADE} set, kills don't move them up: they upgrade like any other unit, which needs {LOC_RESOURCE_IRON_NAME}.
